## 4a3ababcaceb

**Finding 1 — canonical-fitting “largest motif” shortcut is never challenged.** A rival can ignore color-2 authority, choose the non-target tile with the greatest number of nonzero cells (row-major first on ties), and copy that shape in color 8. It matches all 3/3 canonical pairs and 40/40 sampled ordinary outputs under protected Racket. Ordinary generation makes the shortcut reliable: source tiles have 4–6 nonzero red cells, while decoy tiles have at most one nonzero cell; in 80 draws, max decoy mass was 0 once and 1 seventy-nine times.

The target generator's `self_check` accepts this exact input, where a four-cell color-1 decoy is denser than the three-cell red source:

```text
22090009110
20090309110
00090009000
```

The intended Racket rule copies the color-2 source:

```text
22098809110
20098009110
00090009000
```

The rival copies the denser color-1 decoy and incorrectly paints the target center:

```text
22098809110
20098809110
00090009000
```

**Finding 2 — ordinary profiles exclude every canonical lattice height and `src_size` is a dead declared control.** All three canonical inputs are 3x11 one-row/three-column lattices. Across 80 ordinary medium draws, profiles were only 2x3, 2x4, 3x3, or 3x4 tile lattices; none had one tile row. Calling `generate(..., src_size=9)` produced only four red source cells, proving the declared `src_size` override is ignored.
